Freixas et al. 2012 article abstract and authorized Oxford interrupted status
correctness.rationale: A complete independent enumeration of all nonempty antichains of subsets of n players and their induced proper monotone simple games was performed for n=1,2,3,4,5, using exact rational arithmetic for Johnston scores and integer critical-winning-coalition counts for Banzhaf. Proper labeled counts are exactly 1,3,11,80,2645; weak ranking disagreements are 0 through n=4 and 480 at n=5. Among the 480, no strict Banzhaf pair comparison reverses under Johnston: 420 games refine two unordered pairs and 60 refine four. Canonicalization of all five-player divergent minimal-winning antichains under 120 player permutations yields precisely nine classes, seven orbit-60 and two orbit-30. This independently reproduces the pinned package's exact exhaustive finite proof domain and the listed representative scores, with strict properness and both weak rank ties tested. There is no extrapolation to six players or non-proper games.
residual_risks: Scope includes proper simple games only and weak rankings, not numeric power-vector distances.
The proof is finite and exhaustive at n≤5, not an unrestricted classification.

evidence: Freixas semicomplete class forces ordinal equivalence but properness does not imply semicompleteness. Universal Resultary cutoff implies agreement at n≤4; it does not determine how many proper n=5 examples disagree.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader prior claim dominates the first-cutoff part but does not determine the new proper-qualitative census; no false novelty of covered corollary.

originality.rationale: Published Resultary October 4, 2026 proves the strictly broader *qualitative* five-player Johnston/Banzhaf separation boundary for all simple games, as well as the 34 of 208 isomorphism-class unrestricted census and the unique sparsest three-minimal-winner witness. Therefore the naked five-player cutoff is ALREADY COVERED and is not claimed original here. What survives is the motivated quantitative classification of the proper subclass: exactly 480/2645 first-layer discrepancies, precisely nine symmetry classes and the new structural tie-refinement/no-strict-reversal property. The October 4 full RESULT.md was inspected and does not contain these restricted counts. Freixas's full 2011 presentation gives the formulas and semicomplete equivalence theorem; the inaccessible 2012 full journal paper may contain further examples/tables, so only best-of-knowledge priority for the *proper exact census* is asserted.
residual_risks: The earlier published general five-player cutoff fully covers the *qualitative* minimal-size sentence; only the additional proper-class count/orbit and tie refinement receive originality credit.
Freixas–Marciniak–Pons (2012) full article was not accessible without interactive verification (Oxford reported interrupted); it may contain previously unindexed proper-game examples or census.

value.rationale: Properness is a fundamental condition on voting games, independent of semicompleteness. An exact first-disagreement census within that natural subclass answers how often two classical criticality indices disagree and whether the disagreement is a strict reversal or only tie-splitting; classifying precisely nine symmetry types and 96/529 incidence gives a reusable benchmark for voting-power theory. Its value rests on these previously unrecorded finer statistics, not on repeating the covered five-player cutoff.
residual_risks: Finite n≤5 classification; cannot infer behavior in larger proper games or general strict-reversal impossibility.
Qualitative first-size statement already belongs to earlier published unrestricted classification.

limitations: Accepted novelty only for proper five-player quantitative nine-class and tie-refinement classification; published unrestricted first-size cutoff is PRIOR ART; journal article full-text access unresolved.
